result.title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
result.summary: Reinforcement learning sharpens LLM reasoning, but parameter updates are expensive, forgetful, and opaque; training-free libraries swap gradients for a textual store but still use trajectory-level, correlation-based admission and flat structure. To address both, we propose HyperSkill, a Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO framework that keeps the backbone frozen and replaces gradient updates with auditable edits to a Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library, where skills are advantage-bearing nodes and compositions are hyperedges. It has three components: training-time distillation admits counterfactually checked skills and learns a protocol skill from failures; gated hypergraph retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills where a per-dataset gate admits them; and an execution protocol makes the frozen backbone commit to an answer. On 11 text, vision-language, and omnimodal benchmarks, HyperSkill is best or tied on every dataset and beats the best baseline by 13.0 average F1 points while keeping the backbone frozen. Our software and data are publicly available at https://github.com/LHRLAB/HyperSkill.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 HyperSkill：冻结主干，以超图索引的技能库（技能为携带优势值的节点、组合为超边）替代梯度更新，配合反事实检验的技能准入、门控超图检索与执行协议，并在 11 个文本、视觉语言与全模态基准上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反事实检验的技能准入」与按数据集门控的技能注入，可能为 LVR 中免梯度的轨迹监督、贡献分配及「答案是否真正使用注入内容」的核查提供可借鉴线索；但方法停留在文本技能层，未涉及内部 latent 状态，需进一步核查。
